chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with the one in Ihraam entering the bathhouse, but he should not massage (his body).

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihraam (consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihraam take a bath and massage their body?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies the distinction between general cleansing and the specific act of vigorous scrubbing (tadalluk), which is often associated with removing hair or sweat in a manner that might imply shedding the state of Ihraam. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the pilgrimage state while allowing for necessary hygiene, distinguishing between mere washing and the more intensive act of exfoliation.
